title.zh: 卷一百七十七 列傳第一百二十七: 崔慎由 崔珙 盧鈞 裴休 楊收 韋保衡 路巖 夏侯孜 劉瞻 劉瑑 曹確 畢諴 杜審權 劉鄴 豆盧瑑
title.en: Volume 177 Biographies 127: Cui Shenyou, Cui Gong, Lu Jun, Pei Xiu, Yang Shou, Wei Baoheng, Lu Yan, Xiao Houzi, Liu Zhan, Liu Zhuan, Cao Que, Bi Xian, Du Shenquan, Liu Ye, Dou Luzhan

sentences.zh: 崔慎由，字敬止，清河武城人。

translations.literal: Cui Shenyou, styled Jingzhi, was a native of Wu Cheng in Qinghe.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Shenyou, styled Jingzhi, was a native of Wu Cheng in Qinghe.

sentences.zh: 高祖融，位終國子司業，謚曰文，自有傳。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Rong ended his career as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and was posthumously titled Wen; he has his own biography.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Rong ended his career as Vice Director of the Directorate of Education and was posthumously titled Wen; he has his own biography.

sentences.zh: 曾祖翹，位終禮部尚書、東都留守。

translations.literal: His great-grandfather Qiao ended his career as Minister of Rites and Eastern Capital Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: His great-grandfather Qiao ended his career as Minister of Rites and Eastern Capital Garrison Commander.

sentences.zh: 祖異，位終渠州刺史。

translations.literal: His grandfather Yi ended his career as Prefect of Qu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather Yi ended his career as Prefect of Qu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 父從，少孤貧。

translations.literal: His father Cong was orphaned young and poor.
translations.idiomatic: His father Cong was orphaned young and poor.

sentences.zh: 寓居太原，與仲兄能同隱山林，苦心力學。

translations.literal: He lived in Taiyuan and, with his elder brother Neng, hid together in the mountains and forests, studying with bitter effort.
translations.idiomatic: He lived in Taiyuan and, with his elder brother Neng, withdrew to the mountains and forests, studying with bitter effort.

sentences.zh: 屬歲兵荒，至於絕食。

translations.literal: When famine and warfare came, they even ran out of food.
translations.idiomatic: When famine and warfare came, they even ran out of food.

sentences.zh: 弟兄采梠拾橡實，飲水棲衡；

translations.literal: The brothers gathered mulberry leaves and picked acorns, drinking water and dwelling in lean-to shelters;
translations.idiomatic: The brothers gathered mulberry leaves and picked acorns, drinking water and dwelling in lean-to shelters;

sentences.zh: 而講誦不輟。

translations.literal: yet they never stopped lecturing and reciting.
translations.idiomatic: yet they never stopped lecturing and reciting.

sentences.zh: 怡然終日，不出山巖，如是者十年。

translations.literal: They remained content all day long and did not leave the mountain cliffs—for ten years thus.
translations.idiomatic: They remained content all day long and did not leave the mountain cliffs—for ten years thus.

sentences.zh: 貞元初，進士登第，釋褐山南西道推官，府公嚴震，待以殊禮。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving office he became investigating officer of the Shannan West Circuit, and the circuit commissioner Yan Zhen treated him with exceptional courtesy.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Zhenyuan era he passed the jinshi examination; upon leaving office he became investigating officer of the Shannan West Circuit, and the circuit commissioner Yan Zhen treated him with exceptional courtesy.

sentences.zh: 以父優免。

translations.literal: Because of his father's mourning he was exempted from service.
translations.idiomatic: Because of his father's mourning he was exempted from service.

sentences.zh: 弟兄廬於父墓，手植松柏。

translations.literal: The brothers built a hut at their father's tomb and planted pines and cypresses with their own hands.
translations.idiomatic: The brothers built a hut at their father's tomb and planted pines and cypresses with their own hands.

sentences.zh: 免喪，不應辟命。

translations.literal: When mourning ended, he did not respond to summons to office.
translations.idiomatic: When mourning ended, he did not respond to summons to office.

sentences.zh: 久之，西川節度使韋臯開西南夷，置兩路運糧使，奏從掌西山運務，後權知邛州事。

translations.literal: After a long time, the Xichuan Military Commissioner Wei Gao opened relations with the southwestern barbarians and established two grain-transport commissioners; he memorialized that Cong should manage transport affairs on the western mountains, and later Cong was appointed acting Prefect of Qiong.
translations.idiomatic: After a long time, the Xichuan Military Commissioner Wei Gao opened relations with the southwestern barbarians and established two grain-transport commissioners; he memorialized that Cong should manage transport affairs on the western mountains, and later Cong was appointed acting Prefect of Qiong.

sentences.zh: 及臯薨，副使劉辟阻命，欲並東川，以謀告從。

translations.literal: When Gao died, Vice Commissioner Liu Pi defied orders and wished to annex Dongchuan as well; he told Cong of his plan.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao died, Vice Commissioner Liu Pi defied orders and wished to annex Dongchuan as well; he told Cong of his plan.

sentences.zh: 從以書諭辟，辟怒，出兵攻之，從嬰城拒守，卒不從之。

translations.literal: Cong wrote to admonish Pi; Pi grew angry, sent troops to attack him, and Cong held the city and resisted—he never yielded in the end.
translations.idiomatic: Cong wrote to admonish Pi; Pi grew angry, sent troops to attack him, and Cong held the city and resisted—he never yielded in the end.

sentences.zh: 高崇文平蜀，從事坐累多伏法，惟從以拒辟免。

translations.literal: When Gao Chongwen pacified Shu, many staff members were punished by law; only Cong was spared because he had resisted Pi.
translations.idiomatic: When Gao Chongwen pacified Shu, many staff members were punished by law; only Cong was spared because he had resisted Pi.

sentences.zh: 盧坦在宣州，辟為團練觀察副使。

translations.literal: When Lu Tan was at Xuan Prefecture, he summoned Cong as deputy training-and-observation commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: When Lu Tan was at Xuan Prefecture, he summoned Cong as deputy training-and-observation commissioner.

sentences.zh: 元和初入朝，累遷吏部員外郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he entered court and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the Yuanhe era he entered court and was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director in the Ministry of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 九年，裴度為中丞，奏從為侍御史知雜，守右司郎中。

translations.literal: In the ninth year, when Pei Du served as censor-in-chief, he memorialized that Cong should serve as attending censor with mixed duties and hold the post of Right Bureau Director.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth year, when Pei Du served as censor-in-chief, he memorialized that Cong should serve as attending censor with mixed duties and hold the post of Right Bureau Director.

sentences.zh: 度作相，用從自代為中丞。

translations.literal: When Du became chief minister, he used Cong to replace himself as censor-in-chief.
translations.idiomatic: When Du became chief minister, he used Cong to replace himself as censor-in-chief.

sentences.zh: 從氣貌孤峻，正色立朝，彈奏不避權幸。

translations.literal: Cong's bearing was stern and lofty; he stood at court in proper color and impeached without avoiding the powerful and favored.
translations.idiomatic: Cong's bearing was stern and lofty; he stood at court in proper color and impeached without avoiding the powerful and favored.

sentences.zh: 事關臺閣或付仗內者，必抗章論列，請歸有司。

translations.literal: Whenever a matter concerned the censorate or was handed to the palace guard, he always submitted a memorial arguing the point and requested that it be returned to the proper office.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever a matter concerned the censorate or was handed to the palace guard, he always submitted a memorial arguing the point and requested that it be returned to the proper office.

sentences.zh: 選辟御史，必先質重貞退者。

translations.literal: In selecting and recommending censors, he always first sought men of substance, integrity, and restraint.
translations.idiomatic: In selecting and recommending censors, he always first sought men of substance, integrity, and restraint.

sentences.zh: 改給事中，數月，出為陜州大都督府長史、陜虢團練觀察使、兼御史中丞，賜紫金魚袋。

translations.literal: He was reassigned as Supervising Censor, and several months later was sent out as Chief Administrator of the Shaan Prefecture Superior Protectorate, Shaan-Guo Training-and-Observation Commissioner, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and was granted the purple-gold fish pouch.
translations.idiomatic: He was reassigned as Supervising Censor, and several months later was sent out as Chief Administrator of the Shaan Prefecture Superior Protectorate, Shaan-Guo Training-and-Observation Commissioner, and concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and was granted the purple-gold fish pouch.

sentences.zh: 入為尚書右丞。

translations.literal: He entered court as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 淄青賊平，鎮州王承宗懼，上章請割德、棣二州自贖，又令二子入侍。

translations.literal: When the Ziqing rebels were pacified, Wang Chengzong of Zhen Prefecture was afraid; he submitted a memorial requesting to cede De and Di prefectures to redeem himself, and also sent two sons to attend at court.
translations.idiomatic: When the Ziqing rebels were pacified, Wang Chengzong of Zhen Prefecture was afraid; he submitted a memorial requesting to cede De and Di prefectures to redeem himself, and also sent two sons to attend at court.

sentences.zh: 憲宗選使臣宣諭，以從中選。

translations.literal: Emperor Xianzong chose envoys to proclaim the edict; Cong was selected from among them.
translations.idiomatic: Emperor Xianzong chose envoys to proclaim the edict; Cong was selected from among them.

sentences.zh: 議者以承宗罪惡貫盈，每多奸譎，入朝二子，必非血胤，人頗憂之。

translations.literal: Commentators held that Chengzong's crimes filled the measure and he was often treacherous; if the two sons who entered court were not truly his blood, people were much worried.
translations.idiomatic: Commentators held that Chengzong's crimes filled the measure and he was often treacherous; if the two sons who entered court were not truly his blood, people were much worried.

sentences.zh: 從次魏州，田弘正以路由寇境，欲以五百騎援之，從辭之。

translations.literal: Cong stopped at Wei Prefecture; Tian Hongzheng's route passed through bandit territory, and he wished to aid him with five hundred horsemen, but Cong declined.
translations.idiomatic: Cong stopped at Wei Prefecture; Tian Hongzheng's route passed through bandit territory, and he wished to aid him with five hundred horsemen, but Cong declined.

sentences.zh: 以童奴十數騎，徑至鎮州。

translations.literal: With only a dozen or so young servants on horseback, he went straight to Zhen Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: With only a dozen or so young servants on horseback, he went straight to Zhen Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 於鞠場宣敕，三軍大集。

translations.literal: At the drill ground he proclaimed the edict, and the whole army gathered in great numbers.
translations.idiomatic: At the drill ground he proclaimed the edict, and the whole army gathered in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 從諭以逆順，辭情慷慨，軍士感動，承宗泣下，禮貌益恭，遂按德、棣戶口符印而還。

translations.literal: Cong explained the logic of rebellion and loyalty with impassioned words; the soldiers were moved, Chengzong wept, and his courtesy grew still more respectful; Cong then verified the household registers and seals of De and Di and returned.
translations.idiomatic: Cong explained the logic of rebellion and loyalty with impassioned words; the soldiers were moved, Chengzong wept, and his courtesy grew still more respectful; Cong then verified the household registers and seals of De and Di and returned.

sentences.zh: 其年八月，出為興元尹、御史大夫、山南西道節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the eighth month of that year he was sent out as Chief of Xingyuan, Censor-in-Chief, and Shannan West Circuit Military Commissioner and Observer.
translations.idiomatic: In the eighth month of that year he was sent out as Chief of Xingyuan, Censor-in-Chief, and Shannan West Circuit Military Commissioner and Observer.

sentences.zh: 監軍使知上意欲大用之，每為中貴傳達意旨，欲其賂遺，從終不答。

translations.literal: The army supervisor knew the emperor wished to use Cong greatly and often conveyed that intent through palace eunuchs, wanting him to give bribes and gifts; Cong never responded.
translations.idiomatic: The army supervisor knew the emperor wished to use Cong greatly and often conveyed that intent through palace eunuchs, wanting him to give bribes and gifts; Cong never responded.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，召拜尚書左丞。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong acceded, Cong was summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong acceded, Cong was summoned and appointed Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 長慶二年，檢校禮部尚書、鄜州刺史、鄜坊丹延節度等使。

translations.literal: In the second year of Changqing he was appointed Acting Minister of Rites, Prefect of Yan, and Yan-Fang-Dan-Yan Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Changqing he was appointed Acting Minister of Rites, Prefect of Yan, and Yan-Fang-Dan-Yan Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 鄜畤內接畿甸，神策軍鎮相望，逾禁犯法，累政不能制。

translations.literal: Within the Yan region it adjoined the capital circuit; Shence armies were stationed facing one another; they repeatedly violated prohibitions and broke the law, and successive administrations could not control them.
translations.idiomatic: Within the Yan region it adjoined the capital circuit; Shence armies were stationed facing one another; they repeatedly violated prohibitions and broke the law, and successive administrations could not control them.

sentences.zh: 而從撫遏舉奏，軍士惕然。

translations.literal: Yet Cong soothed and restrained them and submitted impeachments, and the soldiers became wary.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Cong soothed and restrained them and submitted impeachments, and the soldiers became wary.

sentences.zh: 党項羌有以羊馬來市者，必先遺帥守，從皆不受，撫諭遣之。

translations.literal: When Tangut tribesmen came to market with sheep and horses, they always first presented gifts to the military commissioner; Cong accepted none of them and sent them away with soothing words.
translations.idiomatic: When Tangut tribesmen came to market with sheep and horses, they always first presented gifts to the military commissioner; Cong accepted none of them and sent them away with soothing words.

sentences.zh: 群羌不敢為盜。

translations.literal: The tribes did not dare become bandits.
translations.idiomatic: The tribes did not dare become bandits.

sentences.zh: 四年，入為吏部侍郎，尋改太常卿。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and soon was reassigned as Minister of Ceremonies.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he entered court as Vice Director of the Ministry of Personnel, and soon was reassigned as Minister of Ceremonies.

sentences.zh: 寶歷二年，檢校吏部尚書，充東都留守。

translations.literal: In the second year of Baoli he was appointed Acting Minister of Personnel and Eastern Capital Garrison Commander.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Baoli he was appointed Acting Minister of Personnel and Eastern Capital Garrison Commander.

sentences.zh: 太和三年，入為戶部尚書。

translations.literal: In the third year of Taihe he entered court as Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year of Taihe he entered court as Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 李宗閔秉政，以從與裴度、李德裕厚善，惡之。

translations.literal: When Li Zongmin held power, because Cong was close to Pei Du and Li Deyu, he disliked him.
translations.idiomatic: When Li Zongmin held power, because Cong was close to Pei Du and Li Deyu, he disliked him.

sentences.zh: 改檢校尚書右僕射、太子賓客，東都分司。

translations.literal: Cong was reassigned Acting Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Crown Prince Guest, serving in the Eastern Capital branch office.
translations.idiomatic: Cong was reassigned Acting Right Vice Director of the Ministry of Works and Crown Prince Guest, serving in the Eastern Capital branch office.

sentences.zh: 從請告百日，罷官，物論咎執政。

translations.literal: Cong requested leave for one hundred days and resigned his office; public opinion blamed those in power.
translations.idiomatic: Cong requested leave for one hundred days and resigned his office; public opinion blamed those in power.

sentences.zh: 宗閔懼，四年三月，召拜檢校左僕射，兼揚州大都督府長史、御史大夫，充淮南節度副大使，知節度事。

translations.literal: Zongmin was afraid; in the third month of the fourth year he summoned Cong and appointed him Acting Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, Chief Administrator of Yang Prefecture Superior Protectorate, Censor-in-Chief, and Deputy Military Commissioner of Huainan, directing military affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Zongmin was afraid; in the third month of the fourth year he summoned Cong and appointed him Acting Left Vice Director of the Ministry of Works, Chief Administrator of Yang Prefecture Superior Protectorate, Censor-in-Chief, and Deputy Military Commissioner of Huainan, directing military affairs.

sentences.zh: 揚府舊有貨曲之利，資產奴婢交易者，皆有貫率，羊有口算，每歲收利以給用，從悉除之。

translations.literal: The Yangzhou headquarters formerly had profits from wine and grain brokerage; for assets, slaves, and servants in trade there were fixed rates, and sheep were taxed by the head—each year the proceeds were collected for expenses; Cong abolished all of them.
translations.idiomatic: The Yangzhou headquarters formerly had profits from wine and grain brokerage; for assets, slaves, and servants in trade there were fixed rates, and sheep were taxed by the head—each year the proceeds were collected for expenses; Cong abolished all of them.

sentences.zh: 舊制，官吏祿俸有布帛加估之給，節度使獨不在此例。

translations.literal: Under the old system, officials' salaries included an added allowance in cloth and silk at appraised value; the military commissioner alone was not included in this rule.
translations.idiomatic: Under the old system, officials' salaries included an added allowance in cloth and silk at appraised value; the military commissioner alone was not included in this rule.

sentences.zh: 從至，一例估折給之。

translations.literal: When Cong arrived, he applied the same appraised allowance to himself as well.
translations.idiomatic: When Cong arrived, he applied the same appraised allowance to himself as well.

sentences.zh: 六年十月，卒於鎮，贈司空，謚曰貞。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of the sixth year he died in his command; he was posthumously granted Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Zhen.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of the sixth year he died in his command; he was posthumously granted Minister of Works and given the posthumous title Zhen.

sentences.zh: 從少以貞晦恭讓自處，不交權利，忠厚方嚴，正人多所推仰。

translations.literal: From youth Cong maintained himself with integrity, modesty, and deference, did not traffic with power and profit, and was honest, loyal, upright, and strict— upright men widely admired him.
translations.idiomatic: From youth Cong maintained himself with integrity, modesty, and deference, did not traffic with power and profit, and was honest, loyal, upright, and strict—upright men widely admired him.

sentences.zh: 階品合立門戟，終不之請。

translations.literal: By rank he was entitled to gate halberds, yet he never requested them.
translations.idiomatic: By rank he was entitled to gate halberds, yet he never requested them.

sentences.zh: 四為大鎮，家無妓樂，士友多之。

translations.literal: Four times he served as commissioner of a great command, yet his household had no singing girls or musicians; scholars and friends greatly esteemed him.
translations.idiomatic: Four times he served as commissioner of a great command, yet his household had no singing girls or musicians; scholars and friends greatly esteemed him.

sentences.zh: 慎由，太和初擢進士第，又登賢良方正制科。

translations.literal: Shenyou, at the beginning of Taihe, passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Exemplary and Upright special examination.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou, at the beginning of Taihe, passed the jinshi examination and also passed the Exemplary and Upright special examination.

sentences.zh: 聰敏強記，宇量端厚，有父風。

translations.literal: Intelligent, quick to remember, dignified in bearing and generous in capacity, he had his father's manner.
translations.idiomatic: Intelligent, quick to remember, dignified in bearing and generous in capacity, he had his father's manner.

sentences.zh: 釋褐諸侯府。

translations.literal: Upon leaving office he served in feudal headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: Upon leaving office he served in feudal headquarters.

sentences.zh: 大中初入朝，為右拾遺、員外郎、知制誥，正拜舍人，召充翰林學士、戶部侍郎。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Dazhong he entered court as Right Reminder, Outer Court Attendant, and Drafting Officer for Proclamations; he was formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Dazhong he entered court as Right Reminder, Outer Court Attendant, and Drafting Officer for Proclamations; he was formally appointed Gentleman of the Secretariat and summoned to serve as Hanlin Academician and Vice Minister of Revenue.

sentences.zh: 再歷方鎮，入朝為工部尚書。

translations.literal: Twice he served as commissioner of a regional command; he entered court as Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: Twice he served as commissioner of a regional command; he entered court as Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 十年，以本官同平章事，兼集賢殿大學士，轉監修國史、上柱國，加太中大夫、兼禮部尚書。

translations.literal: In the tenth year, with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, transferred to Supervisor of the National History and Pillar of State, and was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and concurrent Minister of Rites.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth year, with his existing office he became Associate Chief Minister, Grand Academician of the Hall of Assembled Worthies, transferred to Supervisor of the National History and Pillar of State, and was promoted to Grand Master of Palace Attendance and concurrent Minister of Rites.

sentences.zh: 初，慎由與蕭鄴同在翰林，情不相洽。

translations.literal: At first Shenyou and Xiao Ye were together in the Hanlin Academy, and their feelings did not harmonize.
translations.idiomatic: At first Shenyou and Xiao Ye were together in the Hanlin Academy, and their feelings did not harmonize.

sentences.zh: 及慎由作相，罷鄴學士。

translations.literal: When Shenyou became chief minister, he removed Ye from the academy.
translations.idiomatic: When Shenyou became chief minister, he removed Ye from the academy.

sentences.zh: 俄而鄴自判度支為平章事，恩顧甚隆。

translations.literal: Soon Ye, from directing the Revenue Bureau, became Associate Chief Minister, and imperial favor was very great.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Ye, from directing the Revenue Bureau, became Associate Chief Minister, and imperial favor was very great.

sentences.zh: 鄴引劉瑑同知政事。

translations.literal: Ye brought in Liu Zhuan to share in governing affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Ye brought in Liu Zhuan to share in governing affairs.

sentences.zh: 十二年二月，詔曰：「太中大夫、中書侍郎、兼禮部尚書、同中書門下平章事、監修國史、上柱國、賜紫金魚袋崔慎由，繼美德門，承家貴位，搢紳偉望，禮樂上流。

translations.literal: In the second month of the twelfth year an edict read: "Grand Master of Palace Attendance, Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Rites, Associate Chief Minister, Supervisor of the National History, Pillar of State, and recipient of the purple-gold fish pouch Cui Shenyou inherits a gate of accumulated virtue, holds a family's noble rank, enjoys the great regard of the gentry, and belongs to the upper stream of ritual and music.
translations.idiomatic: In the second month of the twelfth year an edict read, "Grand Master of Palace Attendance, Vice Director of the Secretariat, concurrent Minister of Rites, Associate Chief Minister, Supervisor of the National History, Pillar of State, and recipient of the purple-gold fish pouch Cui Shenyou inherits a gate of accumulated virtue, holds a family's noble rank, enjoys the great regard of the gentry, and belongs to the upper stream of ritual and music.

sentences.zh: 挺松筠之貞姿，服蘭蓀之懿行。

translations.literal: He displays the upright bearing of pine and bamboo and wears the fine conduct of orchid and iris.
translations.idiomatic: He displays the upright bearing of pine and bamboo and wears the fine conduct of orchid and iris.

sentences.zh: 自居名器，累歷清華。

translations.literal: Since holding a famous office he has repeatedly passed through pure and splendid posts.
translations.idiomatic: Since holding a famous office he has repeatedly passed through pure and splendid posts.

sentences.zh: 禁林才擅於多能，綸閣詞推於巨麗。

translations.literal: In the forbidden grove his talent excels in many abilities; in the drafting pavilion his words are praised for great beauty.
translations.idiomatic: In the forbidden grove his talent excels in many abilities; in the drafting pavilion his words are praised for great beauty.

sentences.zh: 物情愈茂，延譽甚高，再列二卿之崇，亟闡六條之化。

translations.literal: Public sentiment grows ever richer and extended praise is very high; twice he has stood among the exalted two ministers and repeatedly has unfolded the transformation of the six principles.
translations.idiomatic: Public sentiment grows ever richer and extended praise is very high; twice he has stood among the exalted two ministers and repeatedly has unfolded the transformation of the six principles.

sentences.zh: 爰加獎任，益委重難。

translations.literal: Now additional reward and appointment are added, and heavy difficulty is entrusted still more.
translations.idiomatic: Now additional reward and appointment are added, and heavy difficulty is entrusted still more.

sentences.zh: 屢啟嘉謨，俄參大柄，而周涉寒暑，備見器能。

translations.literal: Repeatedly he has offered excellent counsel; soon he shared the great handle, and through cold and heat he has fully shown capacity.
translations.idiomatic: Repeatedly he has offered excellent counsel; soon he shared the great handle, and through cold and heat he has fully shown capacity.

sentences.zh: 道已著於始終，思豈殊於中外！

translations.literal: His way has been shown from beginning to end—how could his thought differ between inside and outside!
translations.idiomatic: His way has been shown from beginning to end—how could his thought differ between inside and outside!

sentences.zh: 可檢校禮部尚書、梓州刺史、兼御史大夫、劍南東川節度使。」

translations.literal: He may be appointed Acting Minister of Rites, Prefect of Zi, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of the Eastern Chuan Circuit."
translations.idiomatic: He may be appointed Acting Minister of Rites, Prefect of Zi, concurrent Censor-in-Chief, and Military Commissioner of the Eastern Chuan Circuit."

sentences.zh: 咸通初，改為華州刺史、潼關防禦、鎮國軍等使，加檢校司空、河中尹、河中晉絳節度使。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he was reassigned Prefect of Hua, Defender of Tong Pass, Commander of the Zhenguo Army, and promoted Acting Minister of Works, Chief of the Hezhong Superior Protectorate, and Hezhong-Jin-Jiang Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiantong he was reassigned Prefect of Hua, Defender of Tong Pass, Commander of the Zhenguo Army, and promoted Acting Minister of Works, Chief of the Hezhong Superior Protectorate, and Hezhong-Jin-Jiang Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 入為吏部尚書。

translations.literal: He entered court as Minister of Personnel.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court as Minister of Personnel.

sentences.zh: 移疾請老，拜太子太保，分司東都，卒。

translations.literal: He fell ill and requested retirement; he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince, serving in the Eastern Capital branch office, and died.
translations.idiomatic: He fell ill and requested retirement; he was appointed Grand Mentor of the Crown Prince, serving in the Eastern Capital branch office, and died.

sentences.zh: 子胤。

translations.literal: His son was Yin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yin.

sentences.zh: 弟安潛。

translations.literal: His younger brother was Anqian.
translations.idiomatic: His younger brother was Anqian.

sentences.zh: 安潛，字進之，大中三年，登進士第。

translations.literal: Anqian, styled Jinzhi, in the third year of Dazhong passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Anqian, styled Jinzhi, in the third year of Dazhong passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 咸通中，累歷清顯，出為許州刺史、忠武軍節度觀察等使。

translations.literal: In the Xiantong era he repeatedly held pure and prominent posts and was sent out as Prefect of Xu and Military Commissioner and Observer of the Zhongwu Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the Xiantong era he repeatedly held pure and prominent posts and was sent out as Prefect of Xu and Military Commissioner and Observer of the Zhongwu Army.

sentences.zh: 乾符中，遷成都尹、劍南西川節度等使。

translations.literal: In the Qianfu era he was transferred Chief of Chengdu and Military Commissioner of the Western Chuan Circuit.
translations.idiomatic: In the Qianfu era he was transferred Chief of Chengdu and Military Commissioner of the Western Chuan Circuit.

sentences.zh: 黃巢之亂，從僖宗幸蜀。

translations.literal: During the Huang Chao rebellion he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu.
translations.idiomatic: During the Huang Chao rebellion he followed Emperor Xizong to Shu.

sentences.zh: 王鐸為諸道行營都統，奏安潛為副。

translations.literal: Wang Duo served as overall commander of the circuit armies; he memorialized that Anqian should be his deputy.
translations.idiomatic: Wang Duo served as overall commander of the circuit armies; he memorialized that Anqian should be his deputy.

sentences.zh: 收復兩京，以功累加至檢校侍中。

translations.literal: When the two capitals were recovered, for his merit he was repeatedly promoted to Acting Palace Attendant.
translations.idiomatic: When the two capitals were recovered, for his merit he was repeatedly promoted to Acting Palace Attendant.

sentences.zh: 龍紀初，青州王敬武卒，以安潛代。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Longji, when Wang Jingwu of Qing Prefecture died, Anqian replaced him.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Longji, when Wang Jingwu of Qing Prefecture died, Anqian replaced him.

sentences.zh: 敬武子師範拒命，安潛赴鎮。

translations.literal: Jingwu's son Shifan defied orders; Anqian went to take up his command.
translations.idiomatic: Jingwu's son Shifan defied orders; Anqian went to take up his command.

sentences.zh: 至棣州，刺史張蟾出州兵攻青州，為師範所敗，朝廷竟授之節鉞。

translations.literal: When he reached Di Prefecture, Prefect Zhang Chan led the prefectural troops to attack Qing Prefecture; he was defeated by Shifan, and the court in the end granted Shifan the military commission.
translations.idiomatic: When he reached Di Prefecture, Prefect Zhang Chan led the prefectural troops to attack Qing Prefecture; he was defeated by Shifan, and the court in the end granted Shifan the military commission.

sentences.zh: 安潛還京師，累加太子太傅。

translations.literal: Anqian returned to the capital and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.
translations.idiomatic: Anqian returned to the capital and was repeatedly promoted to Grand Tutor of the Crown Prince.

sentences.zh: 卒，贈太師，謚曰貞孝。

translations.literal: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Zhenxiao.
translations.idiomatic: He died and was posthumously granted Grand Preceptor with the posthumous title Zhenxiao.

sentences.zh: 子柅、艤。

translations.literal: His sons were Ni and Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His sons were Ni and Yi.

sentences.zh: 柅，景福中為起居郎。

translations.literal: Ni, in the Jingfu era, served as Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: Ni, in the Jingfu era, served as Attendant of the Palace Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 艤為右拾遺。

translations.literal: Yi served as Right Reminder.
translations.idiomatic: Yi served as Right Reminder.

sentences.zh: 柅累官至尚書。

translations.literal: Ni rose repeatedly to Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Ni rose repeatedly to Minister.

sentences.zh: 從兄能，少勵誌苦學，累辟使府。

translations.literal: His elder cousin Neng, from youth exerted his will and studied hard, and was repeatedly summoned to headquarters.
translations.idiomatic: His elder cousin Neng, from youth exerted his will and studied hard, and was repeatedly summoned to headquarters.

sentences.zh: 元和初，為蜀州刺史。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he served as Prefect of Shu Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he served as Prefect of Shu Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 六年，轉黔中觀察使。

translations.literal: In the sixth year he was transferred Observer of Qianzhong.
translations.idiomatic: In the sixth year he was transferred Observer of Qianzhong.

sentences.zh: 坐為南蠻所攻，陷郡邑，貶永州刺史。

translations.literal: Because southern barbarians attacked him and cities and districts fell, he was demoted to Prefect of Yong.
translations.idiomatic: Because southern barbarians attacked him and cities and districts fell, he was demoted to Prefect of Yong.

sentences.zh: 穆宗即位，弟從居顯列，召拜將作監。

translations.literal: When Emperor Muzong acceded, because his younger brother Cong held a prominent post, Neng was summoned and appointed Director of Palace Construction.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Muzong acceded, because his younger brother Cong held a prominent post, Neng was summoned and appointed Director of Palace Construction.

sentences.zh: 長慶四年九月，出為廣州刺史、御史大夫、嶺南節度使，卒。

translations.literal: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Changqing he was sent out as Prefect of Guang, Censor-in-Chief, and Lingnan Military Commissioner, and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the ninth month of the fourth year of Changqing he was sent out as Prefect of Guang, Censor-in-Chief, and Lingnan Military Commissioner, and died.

sentences.zh: 子彥曾，有幹局。

translations.literal: His son was Yanzeng, who had administrative ability.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Yanzeng, who had administrative ability.

sentences.zh: 大中末，歷三郡刺史。

translations.literal: At the end of Dazhong he served successively as prefect of three prefectures.
translations.idiomatic: At the end of Dazhong he served successively as prefect of three prefectures.

sentences.zh: 咸通初，累遷太仆卿。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Xiantong he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Xiantong he was repeatedly promoted to Grand Master of the Imperial Stud.

sentences.zh: 七年，檢校左散騎常侍、徐州刺史、御史大夫，充武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: In the seventh year he was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant, Prefect of Xu, and Censor-in-Chief, and served as Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: In the seventh year he was appointed Acting Left Regular Attendant, Prefect of Xu, and Censor-in-Chief, and served as Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army.

sentences.zh: 彥曾通於法律，性嚴急。

translations.literal: Yanzeng was versed in law and stern by nature.
translations.idiomatic: Yanzeng was versed in law and stern by nature.

sentences.zh: 以徐軍驕，命彥曾治之，長於撫養，而短於軍政。

translations.literal: Because the Xu army was insubordinate, Yanzeng was ordered to govern them; he was good at nurturing them but weak in military administration.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Xu army was insubordinate, Yanzeng was ordered to govern them; he was good at nurturing them but weak in military administration.

sentences.zh: 用親吏尹戡、徐行儉當要職。

translations.literal: He put his close clerks Yin Kan and Xu Xingjian in key posts.
translations.idiomatic: He put his close clerks Yin Kan and Xu Xingjian in key posts.

sentences.zh: 二人貪猥，不恤軍旅，士卒怨之。

translations.literal: The two men were greedy and base and did not care for the army; the soldiers resented them.
translations.idiomatic: The two men were greedy and base and did not care for the army; the soldiers resented them.

sentences.zh: 先是，六年，南蠻寇五管，陷交址，詔徐州節度使孟球召募二千人赴援，分八百人戍桂州。

translations.literal: Earlier, in the sixth year, southern barbarians raided the Five Garrisons and captured Jiaozhi; the court ordered Xu Military Commissioner Meng Qiu to recruit two thousand men for relief and assigned eight hundred to garrison Guiz Prefecture.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier, in the sixth year, southern barbarians raided the Five Garrisons and captured Jiaozhi; the court ordered Xu Military Commissioner Meng Qiu to recruit two thousand men for relief and assigned eight hundred to garrison Guiz Prefecture.

sentences.zh: 舊三年一代，至是戍卒求代。

translations.literal: Formerly replacements came every three years; now the garrison soldiers sought relief.
translations.idiomatic: Formerly replacements came every three years; now the garrison soldiers sought relief.

sentences.zh: 尹戡以軍帑匱乏，難以發兵，且留舊戍一年。

translations.literal: Yin Kan, because military funds were exhausted, found it hard to dispatch troops and kept the old garrison for another year.
translations.idiomatic: Yin Kan, because military funds were exhausted, found it hard to dispatch troops and kept the old garrison for another year.

sentences.zh: 其戍卒家人飛書桂林。

translations.literal: The garrison soldiers' families sent urgent letters to Guilin.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison soldiers' families sent urgent letters to Guilin.

sentences.zh: 戍卒怒，牙官許佶、趙可立、王幼誠、劉景、傅寂、張實、王弘立、孟敬文、姚周等九人，殺都頭王仲甫，立糧料判官龐勛為都將。

translations.literal: The garrison soldiers grew angry; the squad officers Xu Ji, Zhao Keli, Wang Youcheng, Liu Jing, Fu Ji, Zhang Shi, Wang Hongli, Meng Jingwen, Yao Zhou, and eight others killed squad chief Wang Zhongfu and made grain officer Pang Xun commander.
translations.idiomatic: The garrison soldiers grew angry; the squad officers Xu Ji, Zhao Keli, Wang Youcheng, Liu Jing, Fu Ji, Zhang Shi, Wang Hongli, Meng Jingwen, Yao Zhou, and eight others killed squad chief Wang Zhongfu and made grain officer Pang Xun commander.

sentences.zh: 群伍突入監軍院取兵甲。

translations.literal: The whole band burst into the army-supervision compound to seize weapons and armor.
translations.idiomatic: The whole band burst into the army-supervision compound to seize weapons and armor.

sentences.zh: 乃剽湘潭、衡山兩縣，虜其丁壯。

translations.literal: They then plundered Xiangtan and Hengshan counties and carried off their able-bodied men.
translations.idiomatic: They then plundered Xiangtan and Hengshan counties and carried off their able-bodied men.

sentences.zh: 乃擅回戈，沿江自浙西入淮南界，由濁河達泗口。

translations.literal: Then on their own they turned their spears about, followed the river from western Zhe to enter Huainan territory, and reached Sizhou by the muddy river.
translations.idiomatic: Then on their own they turned their spears about, followed the river from western Zhe to enter Huainan territory, and reached Sizhou by the muddy river.

sentences.zh: 其眾千余人，每將過郡縣，先令倡卒弄傀儡以觀人情，慮其邀擊。

translations.literal: Their force was more than a thousand men; whenever they were about to pass through a prefecture or county, they first sent soldiers to perform puppet shows to observe public sentiment, fearing interception.
translations.idiomatic: Their force was more than a thousand men; whenever they were about to pass through a prefecture or county, they first sent soldiers to perform puppet shows to observe public sentiment, fearing interception.

sentences.zh: 既離泗口，彥曾令押牙田厚簡慰喻，又令都虞候元密伏兵任山館。

translations.literal: After leaving Sizhou, Yanzeng ordered Adjutant Tian Houjian to offer soothing words, and also ordered Chief Commandant Yuan Mi to set an ambush at Renshan Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: After leaving Sizhou, Yanzeng ordered Adjutant Tian Houjian to offer soothing words, and also ordered Chief Commandant Yuan Mi to set an ambush at Renshan Lodge.

sentences.zh: 龐勛遣吏送狀啟訴，以軍士思歸，勢不能遏，願至府外解甲歸兵。

translations.literal: Pang Xun sent a clerk with a petition stating that the soldiers longed to return home and the momentum could not be checked; he asked to disarm outside the headquarters and return the troops.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun sent a clerk with a petition stating that the soldiers longed to return home and the momentum could not be checked; he asked to disarm outside the headquarters and return the troops.

sentences.zh: 便還家，彥曾怒，誅之。

translations.literal: Then they would go home; Yanzeng was angry and executed them.
translations.idiomatic: Then they would go home; Yanzeng was angry and executed them.

sentences.zh: 勛等擁眾攻宿州，陷之。

translations.literal: Xun and the others led their force to attack Suzhou and captured it.
translations.idiomatic: Xun and the others led their force to attack Suzhou and captured it.

sentences.zh: 出官帑召募。

translations.literal: They opened the official treasury to recruit troops.
translations.idiomatic: They opened the official treasury to recruit troops.

sentences.zh: 翌日，得兵二千人，乃虜奪舟船五千余艘。

translations.literal: The next day they obtained two thousand troops, then seized more than five thousand boats.
translations.idiomatic: The next day they obtained two thousand troops, then seized more than five thousand boats.

sentences.zh: 步卒在船，騎軍夾岸，鼓噪而進。

translations.literal: Foot soldiers were in the boats while cavalry flanked the banks, advancing with drums and shouts.
translations.idiomatic: Foot soldiers were in the boats while cavalry flanked the banks, advancing with drums and shouts.

sentences.zh: 元密發伏邀之，為賊所敗。

translations.literal: Yuan Mi launched the ambush to intercept them and was defeated by the rebels.
translations.idiomatic: Yuan Mi launched the ambush to intercept them and was defeated by the rebels.

sentences.zh: 時亡命者歸賊如市，彥曾驅城中丁男城守。

translations.literal: At the time fugitives joined the rebels like people going to market; Yanzeng drove the city's adult males to defend the walls.
translations.idiomatic: At the time fugitives joined the rebels like people going to market; Yanzeng drove the city's adult males to defend the walls.

sentences.zh: 九年九月十四日，賊逼徐州。

translations.literal: On the fourteenth day of the ninth month of the ninth year the rebels pressed close to Xuzhou.
translations.idiomatic: On the fourteenth day of the ninth month of the ninth year the rebels pressed close to Xuzhou.

sentences.zh: 十五日後，每旦大霧不開。

translations.literal: After the fifteenth, each morning heavy fog did not lift.
translations.idiomatic: After the fifteenth, each morning heavy fog did not lift.

sentences.zh: 十六日，彥曾並誅逆卒家口。

translations.literal: On the sixteenth Yanzeng executed the families of the mutinous soldiers.
translations.idiomatic: On the sixteenth Yanzeng executed the families of the mutinous soldiers.

sentences.zh: 十七日，昏霧尤甚，賊四面斬關而入。

translations.literal: On the seventeenth the dusk fog was especially thick; the rebels cut through the gates on four sides and entered.
translations.idiomatic: On the seventeenth the dusk fog was especially thick; the rebels cut through the gates on four sides and entered.

sentences.zh: 龐勛先謁漢高祖廟，便入牙城。

translations.literal: Pang Xun first visited the temple of Emperor Gaozu of Han, then entered the headquarters compound.
translations.idiomatic: Pang Xun first visited the temple of Emperor Gaozu of Han, then entered the headquarters compound.

sentences.zh: 監軍張道謹相見，不交一言，乃止大彭館。

translations.literal: Army Supervisor Zhang Daojin met him but exchanged not a single word; Xun then stopped at the Great Peng Lodge.
translations.idiomatic: Army Supervisor Zhang Daojin met him but exchanged not a single word; Xun then stopped at the Great Peng Lodge.

sentences.zh: 收尹戡、徐行儉及判官焦璐、李棁、崔蘊、溫廷皓、韋廷義，並殺之。

translations.literal: He seized Yin Kan, Xu Xingjian, and the secretaries Jiao Lu, Li Lun, Cui Yun, Wen Tinghao, and Wei Tingyi, and had them all killed.
translations.idiomatic: He seized Yin Kan, Xu Xingjian, and the secretaries Jiao Lu, Li Lun, Cui Yun, Wen Tinghao, and Wei Tingyi, and had them all killed.

sentences.zh: 翌日，賊將趙可立害彥曾，龐勛自稱武寧軍節度使。

translations.literal: The next day rebel general Zhao Keli killed Yanzeng; Pang Xun styled himself Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army.
translations.idiomatic: The next day rebel general Zhao Keli killed Yanzeng; Pang Xun styled himself Military Commissioner of the Wuning Army.

sentences.zh: 慎由子胤。

translations.literal: Shenyou's son was Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Shenyou's son was Yin.

sentences.zh: 胤，字昌遐，乾寧二年登進士第。

translations.literal: Yin, styled Changxia, in the second year of Qianning passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: Yin, styled Changxia, in the second year of Qianning passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 王重榮鎮河中，辟為從事。

translations.literal: When Wang Chongrong governed Hezhong, Yin was summoned as staff member.
translations.idiomatic: When Wang Chongrong governed Hezhong, Yin was summoned as staff member.

sentences.zh: 入朝，累遷考功、吏部二員外郎，轉郎中、給事中、中書舍人。

translations.literal: He entered court and was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Attendant in the Ministries of War and Personnel, then transferred to Director and Supervising Censor and Gentleman of the Secretariat.
translations.idiomatic: He entered court and was repeatedly promoted to Outer Court Attendant in the Ministries of War and Personnel, then transferred to Director and Supervising Censor and Gentleman of the Secretariat.

sentences.zh: 大順中，歷兵部、吏部二侍郎，尋以本官同平章事。

translations.literal: In the Datong era he served successively as Vice Minister of War and Personnel, and soon with his existing office became Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: In the Datong era he served successively as Vice Minister of War and Personnel, and soon with his existing office became Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 時王室多故，南北司爭權，鹹樹朋黨，外結籓帥。

translations.literal: At the time the royal house had many troubles; the northern and southern offices contended for power; all alike formed factions and outwardly allied with military commissioners.
translations.idiomatic: At the time the royal house had many troubles; the northern and southern offices contended for power; all alike formed factions and outwardly allied with military commissioners.

sentences.zh: 胤長於陰計，巧於附麗；

translations.literal: Yin was skilled in covert schemes and clever at attaching himself to others;
translations.idiomatic: Yin was skilled in covert schemes and clever at attaching himself to others;

sentences.zh: 外示凝重而心險躁。

translations.literal: outwardly he showed weight and dignity while inwardly he was dangerous and restless.
translations.idiomatic: outwardly he showed weight and dignity while inwardly he was dangerous and restless.

sentences.zh: 自李茂貞、王行瑜怙亂，兵勢不遜，杜讓能、韋昭度繼遭誅戮，而宰臣崔昭緯深結行瑜以自固；

translations.literal: Since Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu relied on disorder and their military power did not yield, Du Rangneng and Wei Zhaodu were successively executed; Chief Minister Cui Zhaowei deeply allied with Xingyu to secure himself;
translations.idiomatic: Since Li Maozhen and Wang Xingyu relied on disorder and their military power did not yield, Du Rangneng and Wei Zhaodu were successively executed; Chief Minister Cui Zhaowei deeply allied with Xingyu to secure himself;

sentences.zh: 而待胤以宗人之分，屢加薦用。

translations.literal: yet toward Yin, as a clansman, he repeatedly recommended and employed him.
translations.idiomatic: yet toward Yin, as a clansman, he repeatedly recommended and employed him.

sentences.zh: 累遷中書侍郎、判戶部事。

translations.literal: Yin was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Revenue Bureau.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was repeatedly promoted to Vice Director of the Secretariat and Director of the Revenue Bureau.

sentences.zh: 昭宗出幸石門，胤與同列徐彥若、王摶等從。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong went out to Shimen, Yin followed with his colleagues Xu Yanruo and Wang Bo.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong went out to Shimen, Yin followed with his colleagues Xu Yanruo and Wang Bo.

sentences.zh: 車駕還宮，加禮部尚書，並賜號「扶危匡國致理功臣」。

translations.literal: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, he was promoted Minister of Rites and granted the title "Meritorious Minister Who Supports the Crisis, Restores the State, and Brings Order."
translations.idiomatic: When the imperial carriage returned to the palace, he was promoted Minister of Rites and granted the title "Meritorious Minister Who Supports the Crisis, Restores the State, and Brings Order."

sentences.zh: 三年，李茂貞犯京師，扈昭宗幸華州。

translations.literal: In the third year Li Maozhen attacked the capital; Yin accompanied Emperor Zhaozong to Hua.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Li Maozhen attacked the capital; Yin accompanied Emperor Zhaozong to Hua.

sentences.zh: 帝復雪杜讓能、韋昭度、李磎之枉；

translations.literal: The emperor again cleared the injustice of Du Rangneng, Wei Zhaodu, and Li Qi;
translations.idiomatic: The emperor again cleared the injustice of Du Rangneng, Wei Zhaodu, and Li Qi;

sentences.zh: 懲昭緯之前慝，罷胤政事，檢校兵部尚書、廣州刺史、嶺南東道節度等使。

translations.literal: to punish Zhaowei's earlier wickedness, Yin was removed from governing affairs and appointed Acting Minister of War, Prefect of Guang, and Lingnan East Circuit Military Commissioner.
translations.idiomatic: to punish Zhaowei's earlier wickedness, Yin was removed from governing affairs and appointed Acting Minister of War, Prefect of Guang, and Lingnan East Circuit Military Commissioner.

sentences.zh: 時朱全忠方霸於關東，胤密致書全忠求援。

translations.literal: At the time Zhu Quanzhong was just then dominating east of the Pass; Yin secretly sent a letter to Quanzhong seeking aid.
translations.idiomatic: At the time Zhu Quanzhong was just then dominating east of the Pass; Yin secretly sent a letter to Quanzhong seeking aid.

sentences.zh: 全忠上疏理胤之功，不可離輔弼之地。

translations.literal: Quanzhong submitted a memorial vindicating Yin's merit and saying he could not be removed from the place of chief minister.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong submitted a memorial vindicating Yin's merit and saying he could not be removed from the place of chief minister.

sentences.zh: 胤已至湖南，復召拜平章事。

translations.literal: Yin had already reached Hunan when he was again summoned and appointed Associate Chief Minister.
translations.idiomatic: Yin had already reached Hunan when he was again summoned and appointed Associate Chief Minister.

sentences.zh: 胤既獲汴州之援，頗弄威權。

translations.literal: Once Yin had obtained aid from Bian Prefecture, he played with power quite freely.
translations.idiomatic: Once Yin had obtained aid from Bian Prefecture, he played with power quite freely.

sentences.zh: 恨徐彥若、王摶發昭緯前事，深排抑之。

translations.literal: He resented Xu Yanruo and Wang Bo for exposing Zhaowei's earlier affair and deeply suppressed them.
translations.idiomatic: He resented Xu Yanruo and Wang Bo for exposing Zhaowei's earlier affair and deeply suppressed them.

sentences.zh: 俄出彥為南海節度。

translations.literal: Soon Yanruo was sent out as Military Commissioner of the Southern Sea.
translations.idiomatic: Soon Yanruo was sent out as Military Commissioner of the Southern Sea.

sentences.zh: 又摭王摶交結敕使，同危宗社，令全忠上疏論之。

translations.literal: Yin also gathered evidence that Wang Bo had colluded with edict commissioners and together endangered the altars of soil and grain, and had Quanzhong submit a memorial on the matter.
translations.idiomatic: Yin also gathered evidence that Wang Bo had colluded with edict commissioners and together endangered the altars of soil and grain, and had Quanzhong submit a memorial on the matter.

sentences.zh: 光化中，貶摶溪州司馬，賜死於藍田驛。

translations.literal: In the Guanghua era Bo was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Xi Prefecture and ordered to die at Lantian Post.
translations.idiomatic: In the Guanghua era Bo was demoted to Assistant Administrator of Xi Prefecture and ordered to die at Lantian Post.

sentences.zh: 誅中尉宋道弼、景務修。

translations.literal: Chief Eunuch Song Daobi and Jing Wuxiu were executed.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Eunuch Song Daobi and Jing Wuxiu were executed.

sentences.zh: 自是朝廷權政，皆歸於己，兼領三司使務。

translations.literal: From then on court power and government all belonged to himself, and he concurrently directed the Three Offices.
translations.idiomatic: From then on court power and government all belonged to himself, and he concurrently directed the Three Offices.

sentences.zh: 宦官側目，不勝其忿。

translations.literal: The eunuchs looked askance and could not contain their rage.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs looked askance and could not contain their rage.

sentences.zh: 及劉季述幽昭宗於東內，以德王監國。

translations.literal: When Liu Jishu imprisoned Emperor Zhaozong in the Eastern Inner Palace and had the Virtuous Prince oversee the state,
translations.idiomatic: When Liu Jishu imprisoned Emperor Zhaozong in the Eastern Inner Palace and had the Virtuous Prince oversee the state,

sentences.zh: 季述畏全忠之強，不敢殺胤，但罷知政事，落使務，守本官而已。

translations.literal: Jishu feared Quanzhong's strength and did not dare kill Yin, but only removed him from governing affairs and stripped his commission duties, leaving him in his original office.
translations.idiomatic: Jishu feared Quanzhong's strength and did not dare kill Yin, but only removed him from governing affairs and stripped his commission duties, leaving him in his original office.

sentences.zh: 胤復致書於全忠，請出師反正。

translations.literal: Yin again sent a letter to Quanzhong requesting that troops be dispatched to restore the proper order.
translations.idiomatic: Yin again sent a letter to Quanzhong requesting that troops be dispatched to restore the proper order.

sentences.zh: 故全忠令大將張存敬急攻晉絳河中。

translations.literal: Therefore Quanzhong ordered General Zhang Cunjing to attack Jin and Jiang in Hezhong urgently.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Quanzhong ordered General Zhang Cunjing to attack Jin and Jiang in Hezhong urgently.

sentences.zh: 胤以天子幽囚，諸侯觀釁，有神策軍巡使孫德昭者，頗怒季述之廢立，胤伺知之，令判官石戩與德昭遊，伺其深意。

translations.literal: Because the Son of Heaven was imprisoned and the feudal lords watched for openings, there was Sun Dezhao, patrol commissioner of the Shence Army, who was quite angry at Jishu's deposition and enthronement; Yin, learning this, had his secretary Shi Zhan associate with Dezhao and probe his deeper intent.
translations.idiomatic: Because the Son of Heaven was imprisoned and the feudal lords watched for openings, there was Sun Dezhao, patrol commissioner of the Shence Army, who was quite angry at Jishu's deposition and enthronement; Yin, learning this, had his secretary Shi Zhan associate with Dezhao and probe his deeper intent.

sentences.zh: 每酒酣，德昭泣下，戩知其誠，乃與之謀曰：「今中外大臣，自廢立已來，無不含怒。

translations.literal: Whenever they were deep in wine Dezhao wept; Zhan knew his sincerity and plotted with him, saying, "Now inside and outside, since the deposition and enthronement none have been without anger.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever they were deep in wine Dezhao wept; Zhan knew his sincerity and plotted with him, saying, "Now inside and outside, since the deposition and enthronement none have been without anger.

sentences.zh: 至於軍旅，亦懷憤惋。

translations.literal: As for the armies, they too harbor resentment and indignation.
translations.idiomatic: As for the armies, they too harbor resentment and indignation.

sentences.zh: 今謀反者，獨季述、仲先耳。

translations.literal: Those who now plot rebellion are only Jishu and Zhongxian.
translations.idiomatic: Those who now plot rebellion are only Jishu and Zhongxian.

sentences.zh: 足下誅此二豎，復帝寶位，垂名萬代，今正其時。

translations.literal: If you, sir, execute these two villains, restore the emperor's precious throne, and leave your name for ten thousand generations—now is exactly the time.
translations.idiomatic: If you, sir, execute these two villains, restore the emperor's precious throne, and leave your name for ten thousand generations—now is exactly the time.

sentences.zh: 持疑不斷，則功落他人之手也！」

translations.literal: If you hold back in doubt, the merit will fall into another's hands!"
translations.idiomatic: If you hold back in doubt, the merit will fall into another's hands!"

sentences.zh: 德昭謝曰：「予軍吏耳，社稷大計，不敢自專。

translations.literal: Dezhao declined, saying, "I am but a military clerk; on the great plan of the altars of soil and grain I dare not decide alone.
translations.idiomatic: Dezhao declined, saying, "I am but a military clerk; on the great plan of the altars of soil and grain I dare not decide alone.

sentences.zh: 如相公委使，不敢避也。」

translations.literal: If the Chief Minister entrusts the mission to me, I dare not avoid it."
translations.idiomatic: If the Chief Minister entrusts the mission to me, I dare not avoid it."

sentences.zh: 胤乃割衣帶，手書以通其意。

translations.literal: Yin then cut his belt sash and wrote by hand to communicate his intent.
translations.idiomatic: Yin then cut his belt sash and wrote by hand to communicate his intent.

sentences.zh: 十二月晦，德昭伏兵誅季述。

translations.literal: On the last day of the twelfth month Dezhao set an ambush and executed Jishu.
translations.idiomatic: On the last day of the twelfth month Dezhao set an ambush and executed Jishu.

sentences.zh: 昭宗反正，胤進位司空，復知政事，兼領度支、鹽鐵、三司等使。

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong was restored to the throne, Yin was promoted Minister of Works, again directed governing affairs, and concurrently directed the Revenue, Salt, and Iron, and Three Offices commissions.
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong was restored to the throne, Yin was promoted Minister of Works, again directed governing affairs, and concurrently directed the Revenue, Salt, and Iron, and Three Offices commissions.

sentences.zh: 明年夏，朱全忠攻陷河中、晉絳，進兵至同華。

translations.literal: The next summer Zhu Quanzhong captured Hezhong and Jin-Jiang and advanced his army to Tong and Hua.
translations.idiomatic: The next summer Zhu Quanzhong captured Hezhong and Jin-Jiang and advanced his army to Tong and Hua.

sentences.zh: 中尉韓全誨以胤交結全忠，慮汴軍逼京師，請罷知政事，落使務。

translations.literal: Chief Eunuch Han Quanhui, because Yin had allied with Quanzhong and feared Bian troops would press the capital, requested that Yin be removed from governing affairs and stripped of commission duties.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Eunuch Han Quanhui, because Yin had allied with Quanzhong and feared Bian troops would press the capital, requested that Yin be removed from governing affairs and stripped of commission duties.

sentences.zh: 其年冬，全誨挾帝幸鳳翔。

translations.literal: That winter Quanhui took the emperor to Fengxiang.
translations.idiomatic: That winter Quanhui took the emperor to Fengxiang.

sentences.zh: 胤怨帝廢黜，不扈從，遣使告全忠，請於岐陽迎駕，令太子太師盧知猷率百官迎全忠入京師。

translations.literal: Yin resented the emperor's deposition and did not accompany him; he sent envoys to tell Quanzhong, asking that the imperial carriage be welcomed at Qiyang and ordering Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince Lu Zhiyou to lead the hundred officials to welcome Quanzhong into the capital.
translations.idiomatic: Yin resented the emperor's deposition and did not accompany him; he sent envoys to tell Quanzhong, asking that the imperial carriage be welcomed at Qiyang and ordering Grand Preceptor of the Crown Prince Lu Zhiyou to lead the hundred officials to welcome Quanzhong into the capital.

sentences.zh: 初，全忠至華州，遣掌書記裴鑄人奏鳳翔，言欲以兵士迎駕。

translations.literal: At first, when Quanzhong reached Hua, he sent Secretary Pei Zhu to enter court at Fengxiang, saying he wished to use soldiers to welcome the imperial carriage.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when Quanzhong reached Hua, he sent Secretary Pei Zhu to enter court at Fengxiang, saying he wished to use soldiers to welcome the imperial carriage.

sentences.zh: 及入京師，又上表曰：

translations.literal: And on entering the capital he also submitted a memorial saying:
translations.idiomatic: And on entering the capital he also submitted a memorial saying:

sentences.zh: 昭宗得全忠表，怒胤尤甚。

translations.literal: When Zhaozong received Quanzhong's memorial he was furious with Yin above all.
translations.idiomatic: When Zhaozong received Quanzhong's memorial he was furious with Yin above all.

sentences.zh: 是月二十六日詔曰：

translations.literal: On the twenty-sixth day of that month an edict read:
translations.idiomatic: On the twenty-sixth day of that month an edict read:

sentences.zh: 朕以庶士流散，兵革繁多，遂命宰臣，與之商議。

translations.literal: Because the common people were scattered and warfare was abundant, We ordered the chief ministers to consult with them.
translations.idiomatic: Because the common people were scattered and warfare was abundant, We ordered the chief ministers to consult with them.

sentences.zh: 五降內使，一貢表章，堅臥不來，拒召如此。

translations.literal: Five times inner envoys were sent down and once a memorial was submitted, yet he lay abed and would not come, refusing summons thus.
translations.idiomatic: Five times inner envoys were sent down and once a memorial was submitted, yet he lay abed and would not come, refusing summons thus.

sentences.zh: 況又拘留庶吏，廢闕晨趨。

translations.literal: Moreover he detained common clerks and neglected morning attendance.
translations.idiomatic: Moreover he detained common clerks and neglected morning attendance.

sentences.zh: 人既奔驚，朕須巡幸。

translations.literal: People were already alarmed; We had to make a progress.
translations.idiomatic: People were already alarmed; We had to make a progress.

sentences.zh: 果見兵纏輦轂，火照宮闈，煙塵漲天，干戈匝野。

translations.literal: Sure enough troops encircled the imperial carriage and fire lit the palace halls; dust and smoke filled the sky and weapons covered the wilds.
translations.idiomatic: Sure enough troops encircled the imperial carriage and fire lit the palace halls; dust and smoke filled the sky and weapons covered the wilds.

sentences.zh: 致朕奔迫，及於岐陽。

translations.literal: This forced Us to flee in urgency as far as Qiyang.
translations.idiomatic: This forced Us to flee in urgency as far as Qiyang.

sentences.zh: 翠輦未安，鐵騎旋至，圍逼行在，焚燒屋廬。

translations.literal: The jade carriage was not yet settled when iron cavalry soon arrived, besieging the traveling palace and burning dwellings.
translations.idiomatic: The jade carriage was not yet settled when iron cavalry soon arrived, besieging the traveling palace and burning dwellings.

sentences.zh: 睹此阽危，咎將誰執？

translations.literal: Seeing this imminent peril—whose fault shall bear the blame?
translations.idiomatic: Seeing this imminent peril—whose fault shall bear the blame?

sentences.zh: 近者全忠章表，兼遣幕吏敷陳，言宰臣繼飛密緘，促其兵士西上，靜詳構扇，孰測苞藏，無功及人，為國生事。

translations.literal: Recently Quanzhong's memorial and the statements his staff clerks laid out said the chief minister repeatedly sent secret letters urging his soldiers west, and on calm examination of incitement and agitation, who can fathom what was hidden within? He brought no merit to others and created trouble for the state.
translations.idiomatic: Recently Quanzhong's memorial and the statements his staff clerks laid out said the chief minister repeatedly sent secret letters urging his soldiers west, and on calm examination of incitement and agitation, who can fathom what was hidden within? He brought no merit to others and created trouble for the state.

sentences.zh: 於戲！

translations.literal: Alas!
translations.idiomatic: Alas!

sentences.zh: 君人之道，委之宰衡，庶務殷繁，豈能親理？

translations.literal: The way of a ruler is to entrust affairs to the chief ministers; the myriad tasks are numerous—how can he personally manage them?
translations.idiomatic: The way of a ruler is to entrust affairs to the chief ministers; the myriad tasks are numerous—how can he personally manage them?

sentences.zh: 盡將機事，付爾主張，負我何多，構亂至此！

translations.literal: We entrusted all critical affairs to your direction—how much have you failed Us, to create disorder to this point!
translations.idiomatic: We entrusted all critical affairs to your direction—how much have you failed Us, to create disorder to this point!

sentences.zh: 仍存大體，不謂無恩。

translations.literal: Yet preserving the larger frame, We cannot say there was no grace.
translations.idiomatic: Yet preserving the larger frame, We cannot say there was no grace.

sentences.zh: 可責授朝散大夫，守工部尚書。

translations.literal: He may be demoted and appointed Grand Master of the Palace for Dispersing Affairs and Minister of Public Works.
translations.idiomatic: He may be demoted and appointed Grand Master of the Palace for Dispersing Affairs and Minister of Public Works.

sentences.zh: 初，天復反正之後，宦官尤畏胤，事無大小鹹稟之。

translations.literal: At first, after the Tianfu restoration, the eunuchs feared Yin above all; in matters large and small they all reported to him.
translations.idiomatic: At first, after the Tianfu restoration, the eunuchs feared Yin above all; in matters large and small they all reported to him.

sentences.zh: 每內殿奏對，夜則繼之以燭。

translations.literal: Whenever he reported in the inner hall at night, candles followed in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever he reported in the inner hall at night, candles followed in succession.

sentences.zh: 常說昭宗請盡誅內官，但以宮人掌內司事。

translations.literal: He often urged Zhaozong to execute all inner officials and let only palace women manage inner affairs.
translations.idiomatic: He often urged Zhaozong to execute all inner officials and let only palace women manage inner affairs.

sentences.zh: 中尉韓全誨、張弘彥、袁易簡等伺知之，於帝前求哀請命，乃詔胤密事進囊封，勿更口奏。

translations.literal: Chief Eunuchs Han Quanhui, Zhang Hongyan, and Yuan Yijian learned of this and begged for mercy before the emperor; then an edict ordered that Yin's secret affairs be submitted in sealed pouches and no longer reported orally.
translations.idiomatic: Chief Eunuchs Han Quanhui, Zhang Hongyan, and Yuan Yijian learned of this and begged for mercy before the emperor; then an edict ordered that Yin's secret affairs be submitted in sealed pouches and no longer reported orally.

sentences.zh: 宦官無由知其謀，乃求知書美婦人進內，以偵陰事。

translations.literal: The eunuchs had no way to know his plans, so they sought literate beautiful women to enter the inner palace to spy on covert affairs.
translations.idiomatic: The eunuchs had no way to know his plans, so they sought literate beautiful women to enter the inner palace to spy on covert affairs.

sentences.zh: 由是胤謀頗泄。

translations.literal: Because of this Yin's plans leaked quite a bit.
translations.idiomatic: Because of this Yin's plans leaked quite a bit.

sentences.zh: 宦官每相聚流涕，愈不自安。

translations.literal: Whenever the eunuchs gathered they wept together and grew ever more ill at ease.
translations.idiomatic: Whenever the eunuchs gathered they wept together and grew ever more ill at ease.

sentences.zh: 故全誨等為劫幸之謀，由胤忌嫉之太過也。

translations.literal: Therefore Quanhui and the others made the plan to seize the emperor by force—because Yin's jealousy and hatred had gone too far.
translations.idiomatic: Therefore Quanhui and the others made the plan to seize the emperor by force—because Yin's jealousy and hatred had gone too far.

sentences.zh: 及全忠攻鳳翔，胤寓居華州，為全忠畫圖王之策。

translations.literal: When Quanzhong attacked Fengxiang, Yin lodged at Hua and drew up plans for Quanzhong to become king.
translations.idiomatic: When Quanzhong attacked Fengxiang, Yin lodged at Hua and drew up plans for Quanzhong to become king.

sentences.zh: 天復二年，全忠自岐下還河中，胤迎謁於渭橋，捧卮上壽，持板為全忠唱歌，仍自撰歌辭，贊其功業。

translations.literal: In the second year of Tianfu Quanzhong returned from below Qi to Hezhong; Yin went to meet him at Wei Bridge, raised a cup to offer longevity, held a clapper and sang for Quanzhong, and himself composed the lyrics praising his achievements.
translations.idiomatic: In the second year of Tianfu Quanzhong returned from below Qi to Hezhong; Yin went to meet him at Wei Bridge, raised a cup to offer longevity, held a clapper and sang for Quanzhong, and himself composed the lyrics praising his achievements.

sentences.zh: 三年，李茂貞殺韓全誨等，與全忠通和，昭宗急詔征胤赴行在。

translations.literal: In the third year Li Maozhen killed Han Quanhui and the others and made peace with Quanzhong; Emperor Zhaozong urgently edicted Yin to come to the traveling palace.
translations.idiomatic: In the third year Li Maozhen killed Han Quanhui and the others and made peace with Quanzhong; Emperor Zhaozong urgently edicted Yin to come to the traveling palace.

sentences.zh: 凡四降詔，三賜朱書禦劄，稱病不赴。

translations.literal: Four edicts were sent down in all and the vermilion imperial letter was bestowed three times; he claimed illness and did not go.
translations.idiomatic: Four edicts were sent down in all and the vermilion imperial letter was bestowed three times; he claimed illness and did not go.

sentences.zh: 及帝出鳳翔，胤乃迎於中路，即日降制，復舊官，知政事，進位司徒，兼判六軍諸衛事。

translations.literal: When the emperor left Fengxiang, Yin met him on the road; that same day an edict restored his old office and governing affairs, and he was promoted Minister of Education and concurrently Director of the Six Armies and Guard Offices.
translations.idiomatic: When the emperor left Fengxiang, Yin met him on the road; that same day an edict restored his old office and governing affairs, and he was promoted Minister of Education and concurrently Director of the Six Armies and Guard Offices.

sentences.zh: 仍詔移家入左軍，賜帳幄器用十車。

translations.literal: An edict also ordered his family to move into the Left Army and granted ten carts of tents and utensils.
translations.idiomatic: An edict also ordered his family to move into the Left Army and granted ten carts of tents and utensils.

sentences.zh: 胤奏京兆尹鄭元規為六軍副使。

translations.literal: Yin memorialized that Chief of the Capital Zheng Yuangui should serve as deputy director of the Six Armies.
translations.idiomatic: Yin memorialized that Chief of the Capital Zheng Yuangui should serve as deputy director of the Six Armies.

sentences.zh: 胤與全忠奏罷左右神策、內諸司等使及諸道監軍、副監、小使。

translations.literal: Yin and Quanzhong memorialized to abolish the Left and Right Shence and inner-office commissioners and the army supervisors, deputy supervisors, and minor agents of all circuits.
translations.idiomatic: Yin and Quanzhong memorialized to abolish the Left and Right Shence and inner-office commissioners and the army supervisors, deputy supervisors, and minor agents of all circuits.

sentences.zh: 內官三百余人，同日斬之於內侍省。

translations.literal: More than three hundred inner officials were beheaded the same day in the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: More than three hundred inner officials were beheaded the same day in the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 諸道監軍，隨處斬首以聞。

translations.literal: Army supervisors everywhere were beheaded and reported.
translations.idiomatic: Army supervisors everywhere were beheaded and reported.

sentences.zh: 昭宗初幸鳳翔，命盧光啟、韋貽範、蘇檢等作相；

translations.literal: When Emperor Zhaozong first went to Fengxiang, he ordered Lu Guangqi, Wei Yifan, and Su Jian to serve as chief ministers;
translations.idiomatic: When Emperor Zhaozong first went to Fengxiang, he ordered Lu Guangqi, Wei Yifan, and Su Jian to serve as chief ministers;

sentences.zh: 及還京，胤皆貶斥之。

translations.literal: when he returned to the capital Yin had them all demoted and expelled.
translations.idiomatic: when he returned to the capital Yin had them all demoted and expelled.

sentences.zh: 又貶陸扆為沂王傅，王溥太子賓客，學士薛貽矩夔州司戶，韓偓濮州司戶，姚洎景王府咨議。

translations.literal: He also demoted Lu Yi to Tutor of the Prince of Qi, Wang Pu to Crown Prince Guest, Academician Xue Yiju to Assistant Administrator of Kuai Prefecture, Han Wo to Assistant Administrator of Pu Prefecture, and Yao Ji to Consultant of the Prince of Jing's household.
translations.idiomatic: He also demoted Lu Yi to Tutor of the Prince of Qi, Wang Pu to Crown Prince Guest, Academician Xue Yiju to Assistant Administrator of Kuai Prefecture, Han Wo to Assistant Administrator of Pu Prefecture, and Yao Ji to Consultant of the Prince of Jing's household.

sentences.zh: 應從幸群官，貶逐者三十余人。

translations.literal: More than thirty officials who should have accompanied the emperor on the progress were demoted and sent away.
translations.idiomatic: More than thirty officials who should have accompanied the emperor on the progress were demoted and sent away.

sentences.zh: 唯用裴贄為相，以其孤立易制也。

translations.literal: Only Pei Zan was employed as chief minister, because he was isolated and easy to control.
translations.idiomatic: Only Pei Zan was employed as chief minister, because he was isolated and easy to control.

sentences.zh: 內官既盡屠戮，諸使悉罷，天子宣傳詔命，惟令宮人寵顏等宣事。

translations.literal: Once the inner officials had all been slaughtered and the commissioners all abolished, when the Son of Heaven proclaimed edicts only palace women such as Chongyan were ordered to announce affairs.
translations.idiomatic: Once the inner officials had all been slaughtered and the commissioners all abolished, when the Son of Heaven proclaimed edicts only palace women such as Chongyan were ordered to announce affairs.

sentences.zh: 而欺君蠹國，所不忍聞。

translations.literal: Yet deceiving the ruler and ruining the state—what the ear cannot bear to hear.
translations.idiomatic: Yet deceiving the ruler and ruining the state—what the ear cannot bear to hear.

sentences.zh: 胤所悅者阘茸下輩，所惡者正人君子。

translations.literal: Those Yin favored were worthless low fellows; those he hated were upright gentlemen.
translations.idiomatic: Those Yin favored were worthless low fellows; those he hated were upright gentlemen.

sentences.zh: 人人悚懼，朝不保夕。

translations.literal: Everyone was fearful; no one knew he would survive the morning.
translations.idiomatic: Everyone was fearful; no one knew he would survive the morning.

sentences.zh: 其年十月，全忠子友倫宿衛京師，因擊鞠墜馬而卒。

translations.literal: In the tenth month of that year Quanzhong's son Youlun was on palace guard duty in the capital; he fell from a horse while playing cuju and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the tenth month of that year Quanzhong's son Youlun was on palace guard duty in the capital; he fell from a horse while playing cuju and died.

sentences.zh: 全忠愛之，殺會鞠者十余人，而疑胤陰謀，由是怒胤。

translations.literal: Quanzhong loved him, killed more than ten who had joined the game, and suspected Yin of covert plotting—therefore he grew angry with Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong loved him, killed more than ten who had joined the game, and suspected Yin of covert plotting—therefore he grew angry with Yin.

sentences.zh: 初，天子還宮，全忠東歸，胤以事權在己，慮全忠急於篡代，乃與鄭元規謀招致兵甲，以扞茂貞為辭。

translations.literal: At first, when the Son of Heaven returned to the palace Quanzhong went east; because power was in his own hands Yin feared Quanzhong's haste to usurp the throne and plotted with Zheng Yuangui to gather weapons and armor on the pretext of defending against Maozhen.
translations.idiomatic: At first, when the Son of Heaven returned to the palace Quanzhong went east; because power was in his own hands Yin feared Quanzhong's haste to usurp the throne and plotted with Zheng Yuangui to gather weapons and armor on the pretext of defending against Maozhen.

sentences.zh: 全忠知其意，從之。

translations.literal: Quanzhong knew his intent and agreed.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong knew his intent and agreed.

sentences.zh: 胤毀城外木浮圖，取銅鐵為兵仗。

translations.literal: Yin destroyed outer wooden pagodas and took copper and iron to make weapons.
translations.idiomatic: Yin destroyed outer wooden pagodas and took copper and iron to make weapons.

sentences.zh: 全忠令汴州軍人入關應募者數百人。

translations.literal: Quanzhong ordered several hundred Bian Prefecture soldiers entering the Pass to enlist.
translations.idiomatic: Quanzhong ordered several hundred Bian Prefecture soldiers entering the Pass to enlist.

sentences.zh: 及友倫死，全忠怒，遣其子宿衛軍使友諒誅胤，而應募者突然而出。

translations.literal: When Youlun died Quanzhong was enraged and sent his son, the palace guard commissioner Youliang, to execute Yin, while the enlistees burst out suddenly.
translations.idiomatic: When Youlun died Quanzhong was enraged and sent his son, the palace guard commissioner Youliang, to execute Yin, while the enlistees burst out suddenly.

sentences.zh: 四年正月初，貶太子賓客，尋為汴軍所殺。

translations.literal: At the beginning of the first month of the fourth year he was demoted Crown Prince Guest and soon was killed by Bian troops.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of the first month of the fourth year he was demoted Crown Prince Guest and soon was killed by Bian troops.

sentences.zh: 胤傾險樂禍，外示寬宏。

translations.literal: Yin was treacherous and delighted in calamity, outwardly showing broad tolerance.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was treacherous and delighted in calamity, outwardly showing broad tolerance.

sentences.zh: 初拜平章事，其季父安潛謂所親曰：「吾父兄刻苦樹立門戶，一旦終當為緇郎所壞。」

translations.literal: When he first became Associate Chief Minister, his younger uncle Anqian told those close to him, "Our fathers and elder brothers painstakingly established the family gate; in the end it will be ruined by this dark-robed fellow."
translations.idiomatic: When he first became Associate Chief Minister, his younger uncle Anqian told those close to him, "Our fathers and elder brothers painstakingly established the family gate; in the end it will be ruined by this dark-robed fellow."

sentences.zh: 果如其言。

translations.literal: It turned out exactly as he said.
translations.idiomatic: It turned out exactly as he said.

sentences.zh: 胤累加至侍中，封魏國公。

translations.literal: Yin was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.
translations.idiomatic: Yin was repeatedly promoted to Palace Attendant and enfeoffed as Duke of Wei.

sentences.zh: 初，朱全忠雖竊有河南方鎮，憚河朔、河東，未萌問鼎之誌。

translations.literal: At first, though Zhu Quanzhong secretly held the regional commands of Henan, he feared Hebei and Hedong and had not yet conceived the will to seize the throne.
translations.idiomatic: At first, though Zhu Quanzhong secretly held the regional commands of Henan, he feared Hebei and Hedong and had not yet conceived the will to seize the throne.

sentences.zh: 及得胤為鄉導，乃電擊潼關，始謀移國。

translations.literal: Once he had Yin as native guide, he struck Tong Pass like lightning and first plotted to shift the state.
translations.idiomatic: Once he had Yin as native guide, he struck Tong Pass like lightning and first plotted to shift the state.

sentences.zh: 自古與盜合從，覆亡宗社，無如胤之甚也。

translations.literal: Since ancient times none who joined with bandits to overthrow the altars of soil and grain has been worse than Yin.
translations.idiomatic: Since ancient times none who joined with bandits to overthrow the altars of soil and grain has been worse than Yin.

sentences.zh: 子有鄰。

translations.literal: His son was Youlin.
translations.idiomatic: His son was Youlin.

sentences.zh: 崔珙，博陵安平人。

translations.literal: Cui Gong was a native of Anping in Boling.
translations.idiomatic: Cui Gong was a native of Anping in Boling.

sentences.zh: 祖懿。

translations.literal: His grandfather was Yi.
translations.idiomatic: His grandfather was Yi.

sentences.zh: 父颋，貞元初進士登第。

translations.literal: His father Ting, at the beginning of Zhenyuan passed the jinshi examination.
translations.idiomatic: His father Ting, at the beginning of Zhenyuan passed the jinshi examination.

sentences.zh: 元和初累官至少府監。

translations.literal: At the beginning of Yuanhe he rose repeatedly to Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service.
translations.idiomatic: At the beginning of Yuanhe he rose repeatedly to Vice Director of the Palace Domestic Service.

sentences.zh: 四年，出為同州刺史，卒。

translations.literal: In the fourth year he was sent out as Prefect of Tong and died.
translations.idiomatic: In the fourth year he was sent out as Prefect of Tong and died.

sentences.zh: 颋有子八人，皆至達官，時人比漢之荀氏，號曰「八龍」。

translations.literal: Ting had eight sons, all reaching high office; people of the time compared them to the Xun clan of Han and called them the "Eight Dragons."
translations.idiomatic: Ting had eight sons, all reaching high office; people of the time compared them to the Xun clan of Han and called them the "Eight Dragons."

sentences.zh: 長曰琯，貞元十八年進士擢第。

translations.literal: The eldest was Guan, who in the eighteenth year of Zhenyuan passed the jinshi selection.
translations.idiomatic: The eldest was Guan, who in the eighteenth year of Zhenyuan passed the jinshi selection.

sentences.zh: 又制策登科，釋褐諸侯府，入朝為尚書郎。

translations.literal: He also passed the policy examination, left office in a feudal headquarters, and entered court as Director in the Ministry of Revenue.
